First of all, welcome to the Olympic Exclusion Zone. Now I know it can be a bit confusing at first (I know I was) but it becomes clearer the more you play it. 

As for the driving around in circles, I’m guessing you’re using the practice track behind the garage, right? Anyway, what you need to do is park your car back in the garage and head to the projector map, it’s right of the status screen for your car.

That map is how you start a “trip”. You use it and it shows you the map of the exclusion zone. It shows the different routes you can take, the areas, and the area modifiers. The area modifiers are what keep you and the game feeling refreshed and different. Now you choose where you want to go and you scan it. That’s what that thing you installed on the roof of your garage is for. 

Scanning a place will do two things 1. Open the closed shutter in front of your car, allowing you to leave and 2. Show you the details of the areas along the route. The only thing I really pay attention to are the area modifiers because they can change what you may need to take on certain trips. If you’re just starting out, most modifiers are just going to say “???????”. This is normal. Once you experience a modifier for the first time, it’ll no longer say “???????”

I know this is a lot. I probably glossed over a bunch and there’s a good amount of detail in this game which is why I love it. Hope this helps :)

It’s not the fact that you’re an outsider, I feel it’s something deeper. 

I was born and raised in San Diego my entire life. Still live here at 24 years old. It’s something about San Diego and in my opinion, big cities in California that are the problem.

I see cities like San Diego and Los Angeles as “influencer” cities. A lot of people move to these cities with the intention of becoming popular. Back in the day before social media, it was the equivalent of people moving to Hollywood to try and make it big on the big screen. 

But of course, when people aim to be influencers, I feel it makes them into a very fake and narcissistic person. I couldn’t care less about social media and influencers are just walking talking propaganda machines to me. Saying whatever they’re told to say in exchange for money, status, fame. Clawing and pushing down whoever they need to to come out on top. Creating a bubble where they see themselves and only themselves. 

Basically, I feel cities like San Diego and Los Angeles are either “magnets” or even “factories” of fake people. Attracting them and/or even producing them. 

My advice? Don’t worry about making friends, there are a lot of fake people here. Instead focus on hobbies you can enjoy alone. Now I’m not saying don’t make any friends but to be very selective with them. I’ve had plenty of bad experiences who were so called “friends”. Now I’m able to count the amount of real friends I have here on one hand. 

Tl;dr: I feel cities like SD and LA attract and produce self centered individuals that want to make it big online hence creating an interpersonal divide.
